context: Daichi and Tatsuya prepare for the town festival.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: たつや、祭り、本当、もうすぐ。
lines.en: Tatsuya — the festival's almost here. Really something to look forward to.
lines.style: Warm and eager opening, Kansai accent rolling naturally through. Bright, genuine anticipation—not performing it. Soft undercarriage of real affection for the moment and the person.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: うん、本当、皆、本当、楽しみ。
lines.en: Yeah, it really is. Everyone's looking forward to it.
lines.style: Low, measured cadence. No rush. Unhurried warmth that meets Daichi's energy without trying to match it. Gentle, genuine—the ease of someone who doesn't need to fill silence.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.en: The town's really coming back alive with energy.
lines.style: Appreciative brightness in the middle of the thought. Kansai warmth with a soft lift—noticing something good and wanting to share it. Tender undercurrent of hope.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.en: Let's give it our best, together.
lines.style: Patient, collaborative warmth. Low pitch, unhurried. A small commitment offered simply—no drama, just quiet conviction. The kind of statement that lands because it costs something.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.style: Kansai brightness with depth underneath. Gratitude isn't performed or loud; it's steady and real. Soft on the second statement—letting it breathe rather than force it.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.en: It's going to be fun. I know it will be.
lines.style: Low, certain warmth. Not fast—patient with the assurance. Quiet conviction in the trailing edge. The kind of certainty that comes from experience and hope together.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.style: Kansai lilt on the opening, soft and full. The closing moment—genuine, unguarded, tender. No reach for effect, just simple warmth and gratitude allowed to show.
